- If sentiment is high (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.33) and price is rising, model often lags; adjust upward early.
- After sharp spikes in price, model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% above peak.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral, model exhibits mean reversion bias; smooth forecast toward recent mean.
- If true outcome shows strong divergence from forecast in first 5–7 days, reduce forecast slope for next 10 days.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is consistently bullish and price is trending up; increase baseline by 0.5–1.5%.
- If sentiment turns negative after a spike, model often fails to correct; reduce forecast by 1–3% in next 3–5 days.
- Forecast should not exceed 3–5% above recent 10-day average unless sentiment is strongly bullish.
